Canada and the EU are exploring an even deeper alliance — as US ties continue to fray under President Trump.

Andrea Palasciano explains why Canada's relationship could become closer than the UK's. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Treasuries Extend Drop After New Buyback Targets Disappoint
summary: US government bonds fell after the Treasury Department announced target sizes for its expanded buyback program that were lower than some strategists said were possible.

title: Trump’s Latest Trade Threat Weighs on Canadian Firms With US Contracts
summary: Shares of Canadian companies that do business with the US government fell following President Donald Trump’s threat to bar Canadian-origin products from being sold to federal contractors.

title: Dollar Eyes Seven-Month Low as Bessent Remarks Spur Yen Rise
summary: The dollar traded near its lowest level in close to seven months as the yen rallied after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent challenged traders to test his resolve on supporting Japan’s currency.

title: Stocks Fall as Oil Jump, Treasury Plan Lift Yields: Markets Wrap
summary: A resurgence in oil prices hit stocks and bonds, with losses deepening as the Treasury said it will purchase up to $6 billion of longer-dated government debt.

title: Wheat Drops to Two-Week Low Ahead of US Supply, Demand Report
summary: Wheat hit its lowest in two weeks as grain futures were mixed amid geopolitical turmoil and the ahead of the Friday release of a monthly supply and demand report from the US Department of Agriculture.

title: France’s Champagne Quality Seen Exceptional Despite Output Slump
summary: French Champagne output may have been battered by heat waves and drought, but this year’s vintage is shaping up as one of “exceptional quality.”

title: Vale CFO Sees No Downturn in Iron Ore Prices
summary:
Vale SA Chief Financial Officer Marcelo Bacci says iron ore is a resilient commodity and says demand is stable. He also says the mining giant may tap the Chinese bond market in the near future. He speaks on "Bloomberg Open Interest."
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bessent Triples Debt Buyback But Market Shows Disappointment
summary: The US Treasury tripled the initial size of its next buyback of longer-dated government debt, in an announcement that was met with initial disappointment by investors.

title: Gold Trims Gains as Yields Push Higher After Treasury Buyback
summary: Gold trimmed gains as bond yields and the dollar pushed higher after the US Treasury said it will triple its long-dated debt buyback to $6 billion.

title: Apple’s Rally Pressures New CEO to Deliver on Foldable iPhone
summary: Apple Inc.’s $570 billion summer surge is saddling new Chief Executive Officer John Ternus with high expectations heading into the company’s most anticipated event in years: the unveiling of the foldable iPhone on Wednesday.

title: US Firms Unleash Record Wave of Bond Sales in Europe
summary: An unprecedented number of US companies are selling bonds in Europe, drawn by liquidity and attractive terms as their home market strains under a deluge of AI-related debt.

title: US Treasury to Buy Up to $6 Billion in Long-Dated Debt
summary: The US Treasury will purchase up to $6 billion of longer-dated government debt in the first operation under an expanded buybacks program. It's part of Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's effort to stem the rise in borrowing costs. Bloomberg's Michael McKee has the breaking news and immediate market reaction. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Crude Tops $101 as US-Iran War Escalates With Tankers Targeted
summary: Brent oil topped $101 a barrel for the first time since July, as escalating attacks across the Middle East heightened concerns about further disruptions to energy flows out of the crude-rich region.

title: EU Carbon Reform Lead Lawmaker Weighs Smoother Emission Cuts
summary: The European Union’s lead lawmaker on its carbon market reform is considering proposing a smoother pace of emissions cuts next decade in a draft plan due to be unveiled Friday.

title: Europe Gas Prices Rise Above €80 for First Time Since 2023
summary: European natural gas surged above €80 a megawatt-hour for the first time in more than three years, intensifying the threat to the region’s economy as the war in the Middle East drives up energy costs just as winter approaches.

title: South Africa Plans Oil-Refining Revival to Cut Import Dependence
summary: South Africa’s Central Energy Fund outlined plans to revive oil-refining capacity that will see local processing of crude at least triple, potentially reducing dependence on fuel imports.

title: Benfica Investor Dos Santos in Fresh Talks to Sell Stake in Club
summary: Benfica shareholder José António dos Santos said he’s been approached by several investors interested in buying his 16.4% stake in the club after a previous deal fell through.

title: Citizens CEO Says Consumers Are Cautious, But Spending
summary: Citizens Financial Group CEO Bruce Van Saun says the US economy is strong and consumers are spending, but they are cautious. He says customers have figured out how to absorb higher energy costs. He also doesn't expect the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates soon. He speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson Says We're Still in a Bull Market
summary: Morgan Stanley Chief US Equity Strategist Mike Wilson says we're still in a bull market, but higher oil prices and interest rates are a risk to stocks. He says investors should continue to own energy stocks as a hedge. He speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)
